dod_intent_evidence: USAF PLASMA TACFI Phase IIB SBIR, $3,323,650 (2022): their own abstract promises 'a converged identity capability' for 'USAF personnel' (SBIR/STTR record section) — genuine defense motion, but the fielding path for it appears nowhere in their public materials.
score_evidence: 'Consistently ranked at the top of NIST FRTE benchmarks, including 1:1 Verification, 1:N Identification' → lab_language_intensity
'Through rapid software iterations, Paravision reached the top of the National Institute of Science and Technology (NIST) leaderboards' (their own SBIR abstract) → lab_language_intensity
'Runs on Kubernetes, supports REST and gRPC interfaces, and is cloud-ready' — detailed deployment description with zero ATO/RMF/STIG/IL or DDIL language anywhere → deployment_awareness_absence
SBIR abstract mentions Airmen only as mission rhetoric ('the safety and security of our nation's Airmen') — no training, CONOPS, or field-feedback language on any product page → operator_absence
Only live role is 'Senior Solutions Engineer (London Area, GB)' — commercial deployment hiring, no ISSO/compliance/US-gov field role → hiring_profile_skew

blind_spots.blind_spot: Cloud-native container architecture with no visible ATO/RMF path for an Air Force base security system
blind_spots.operator_reality: PLASMA has to run on a government network at an installation — that means RMF accreditation, STIGs, and an IL4/IL5 hosting decision before a single camera goes live; a Kubernetes/gRPC 'cloud-ready' stack scoped for commercial partners restarts that clock from zero, and the TACFI period of performance is the only funding covering it.
blind_spots.why_likely_missing: Their entire commercial motion sells SDKs and containers to integration partners who own deployment; nobody on the public roster owns government accreditation.
blind_spots.evidence_quote: Runs on Kubernetes, supports REST and gRPC interfaces, and is cloud-ready.

blind_spots.blind_spot: 'Real time analytics' across base security domains assumes bandwidth and connectivity a flightline or gate installation may not have
blind_spots.operator_reality: 1:N face search with live video feeds across 'multiple security system domains' is exactly the 30fps-crowd-detection failure mode — constrained base networks and edge enclaves throttle streaming, and without frame-rate/match-rate decoupling the demo that worked in the Presidio lab times out at the gate shack.
blind_spots.why_likely_missing: NIST and DHS rally benchmarks — their entire brag sheet — are run on curated data with unconstrained compute, never over degraded links.
blind_spots.evidence_quote: Through multi-factor authentication and real time analytics, USAF personnel are presented with a converged identity capability

blind_spots.blind_spot: No operator training or sustainment story for the airmen who actually run entry control
blind_spots.operator_reality: The user of a base identity system is an E-3/E-4 security forces airman with minutes of training, enrolling faces in dust, glare, and gloves — enrollment quality in those conditions is what breaks 'ultra-accurate' claims, and nobody in their language trains, fixes, or sustains the system after install.
blind_spots.why_likely_missing: Their customers are solution providers ('Built with Paravision'), so the end operator is two contractual hops away and invisible to them.
blind_spots.evidence_quote: Ultra-accurate face recognition across environments, demographics, and user angles.

opener_hook: Paravision's $3.3M PLASMA TACFI abstract promises USAF personnel real-time converged identity across base security domains, yet every deployment word on paravision.ai is Kubernetes-and-cloud — with no ATO, RMF, or IL-level path mentioned anywhere public.
what_they_do: Commercial face recognition, liveness, and deepfake-detection SDKs, with a USAF TACFI project to field a converged identity system on Air Force installations.
